chapter: Philadelphia bands and the Club Harlem
title: First bass solos and showmanship with Bobby Booker's band
summary: He took slapped solos on Claude Hopkins's theme, wearing a big red hat and spinning the bass, at the Club Harlem in 1934.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Now, had you started doing any solos by then or did you just play in the ensemble? Or did you get solos?

Yeah, I got solos. One of the first solos that I ever did was Claude Hopkin's theme song, 'I Could do Almost Anything For You.' And I used to wear a big red hat and straddle and slap and spin. This was show biz. If you didn't do that -- and I was an up and coming bass player at that time.
Did you do bowing, too, on solos?
Yeah, I knew you could bow. So when you took a solo you just slapped or picked?
